title: Yemen leader announces major military operations against Iran-backed Houthis
gist: Reuters (via Al-Monitor) reports that Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi launched a major Saudi-backed military operation on Oct. 4, 2026 to retake Houthi-held territory, with Saudi Arabia leading air combat and the US providing intelligence; the Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais and hold the initiative after seizing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait — now a key alternative to the effectively closed Strait of Hormuz — and advancing toward besieging Taiz.

insights.claim: Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi announced the start of military operations to retake all Houthi-held territory, saying all opportunities for de-escalation had been exhausted and accusing the Houthis of answering calm with mobilisation and escalation.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Formal end of the 2022 truce framework; expect a prolonged, escalatory conflict on the Arabian Peninsula's southern flank.
insights.quote: Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic

insights.claim: Officials said Saudi Arabia would lead aerial combat while Yemeni forces fight on the ground; the US is already providing intelligence for Riyadh's operations, and some regional and European nations provide mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Direct Saudi involvement raises the likelihood of Houthi retaliation on Saudi energy infrastructure; US intelligence support deepens Washington's entanglement.
insights.quote: The US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen
insights.locator: The US is already providing intelligence

insights.claim: The 2022 truce largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure as a spillover from the Iran war.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The Yemen front is a direct transmission channel from the Iran war into Saudi energy assets.
insights.quote: in a spillover from the Iran war
insights.locator: A truce agreed between the warring parties

insights.claim: The Houthis said they fired ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area, claiming major fires, in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led strikes in 12 hours; Saudi Arabia did not immediately confirm.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Khurais is a major oilfield area; any confirmed damage would add to Gulf supply risk and oil risk premium.

insights.claim: The Houthis maintain the initiative on the ground weeks after seizing the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning coastal offensive that saw government forces collapse.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Houthi control of the Red Sea's southern exit gives them direct leverage over Europe-Asia shipping and Gulf exports routed via the Red Sea.
insights.quote: weeks after seizing the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive down the coast that saw government forces collapse

insights.claim: Bab el-Mandeb has become even more important this year as an alternative route to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed by the Iran conflict.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Both major Gulf export routes now face hostile control, concentrating global energy supply risk and supporting tanker rates and oil prices.

insights.claim: In the last 48 hours Houthis gained strategic hilltops near Taiz and are advancing on the last road between the city and Aden; control of that road would effectively besiege Yemen's third-largest city, home to hundreds of thousands of civilians and thousands of government troops.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A Taiz siege would be a major setback for the government offensive at its outset and worsen the humanitarian crisis.

insights.claim: Analyst Mohammed Al-Qadhi says seizing the western Taiz mountains would let the Houthis protect their rear and consolidate control of the Bab el-Mandeb coast, making recapture much more difficult.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Terrain consolidation implies Houthi chokepoint control could prove durable, prolonging Red Sea shipping risk.

insights.claim: The World Food Programme said three in four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry due to the surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands and disrupted supplies to millions.

insights.so_what: Deepening humanitarian crisis may raise international pressure for a ceasefire.
